intro: The collective is imagined as a loose international network of researchers, artists, educators, and scholars. The profiles below can be edited as the group develops.
heading: Members and Coordinators

items.name: Tomi Slotte Dufva
items.role: Assistant Professor in Arts Education; group coordinator
items.institution: Aalto University, the School of Arts, Design and Architecture, Department of Art and Design
items.researchInterests: Post-digital, post-AI art, education and culture; embodied and experiential learning; critical digital literacy; visual culture; philosophies of art, craft, and education
items.bio: Tomi Slotte Dufva coordinates the group and researches art, education, culture, and technology through post-digital and post-AI perspectives, with attention to embodiment, experience, critical literacy, visual culture, and philosophies of art, craft, and education.

items.name: Member Placeholder 02
items.researchInterests: Post-AI education, critical data studies, feminist data sciences
items.bio: Studies how AI systems shape knowledge practices, pedagogical agency, and the everyday politics of data in educational settings.

items.name: Member Placeholder 03
items.bio: Works with teacher education, craft traditions, and experimental pedagogies that connect material making with cultural analysis.

items.name: Member Placeholder 04
items.researchInterests: Critical technology studies, culture, art, ecological thinking
items.bio: Develops interdisciplinary research environments around artistic inquiry, cultural critique, and technological imaginaries.

items.name: Member Placeholder 05
items.researchInterests: Embodiment, repair cultures, artistic research methods
items.bio: Combines experimental practice, writing, and public pedagogy to examine bodies, tools, infrastructures, and care.

items.name: Member Placeholder 06
items.researchInterests: Digital craft, workshops, participatory methods, media archaeology
items.bio: Facilitates collaborative workshops that use old and new technologies to ask how futures are made, maintained, and refused.
